text:
alex: Heads up — noticed weird tenant metadata showing up in the Insights panel after switching orgs quickly in the console. Repro steps: two tabs, switch org in tab A, open Insights in tab B -> cards from previous org appear briefly.

maria: can repro on staging. looks like prefetch/cache response contains stale org header. quick grab of network: response from /internal/prefetch had header X-Org: org-old even though request had X-Org: org-new.

jamal: ugh, likely cache key scoping issue. i searched the prefetch worker: 
```
const key = `console:prefetch:${userId}`
await redis.set(key, JSON.stringify(payload))
```
no org in key. when user flips org fast the previous payload can be served.

alex: that explains it. also saw billing telemetry where quota usage attributed to wrong org for a handful of requests: `billing.charge.org_id != request.org_id` in last 2 hours. might be upstream fallout.

maria: telemetry note — metric `console.prefetch.cache_hits` shows spike around the same time windows for affected tenants. pinged support, two customers reported transient dashboard data mismatch.

ops-bot: ALERT: 2 incidents flagged (INC-2025-0912,INC-2025-0913) — suspected console data mismatch.

jamal: proposed fixes: 1) include orgId in redis key (console:prefetch:${userId}:${orgId}) 2) add gateway enforcement to strip/validate X-Org on cached responses 3) add unit test + e2e that simulates rapid org switch to prevent regression.

maria: agree. also add a defensive check in prefetch before returning payload: if payload.orgId != request.orgId then discard and miss (to avoid serving wrong org). that's cheap and safe.

alex: migration/backfill: we need to evict old keys that lack org in key. naive script: `redis-cli --scan --pattern "console:prefetch:*"` then inspect values and delete those with mismatched orgs. but be careful with prod traffic.

jamal: draft deletion runbook: 
1) run read-only scan on a replica to collect candidate keys (write down count) 
2) run small-scope purge for high-risk user set (10 users) during low-traffic window 
3) monitor errors/alerts 
4) ramp up purge.

maria: also add a short-term kill-switch feature-flag to disable prefetch for affected orgs so we can mitigate customer impact while patching.

alex: rollout plan: patch prefetch worker + gateway validation, ship to staging, run heavy e2e org-switch test, canary 5% for 1 hour, 25% 6 hours, full rollout. feature flag to disable globally if we see regressions.

jamal: internal-api debate: some folks want gateway to be the single source of truth for header hygiene (strip/normalize), others prefer letting services validate. my take: do both — gateway enforces invariants and services defensively validate. add lint rule in internal-api spec to require `context.orgId` presence when writing caches.

maria: i'll open a quick PR that updates cache key + defensive check + tests. will also add a changelog entry and a short note in rollout checklist about redis purge.

ops-bot: DEPLOYMENT NOTE: staging prefetch v2 build queued #build-789.

alex: telemetry: add alert that tracks `console.prefetch.cache_hits` where `response_org != request_org` (incremental counter). use that to auto-rollback if it spikes.

jamal: one more: check quota-metering path — if billing is consuming `response.org` for attribution, switch to using `request.org` as authoritative until we fully fix cache hygiene. easy fallback.

maria: raising PR now, tests are fast. will tag for review: @jamal @alex.

alex: thanks. once PR is merged i'll coordinate canary with you both and ops. i'll also draft customer comms for the two affected accounts.

jamal: ok, agreed. follow-up items: add unit test in prefetch cache util, add gateway integration test, and add redis purge runbook to ops-runbook.

maria: noted — will update the ops-runbook and include example redis commands (scan+inspect+del) with safety checks.

alex: perfect. marking this thread as actionable. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Reaction: :white_check_mark: added to thread.
